questions.question: Why do Java developers still need to care about memory even though Java has garbage collection?
answer: Because garbage collection does not solve every problem related to data design and object lifecycles.
If you keep references too long, create objects carelessly, or cache things the wrong way, you can still waste memory and create logical memory leaks.
In other words, GC collects garbage automatically, but it does not fix a design that keeps creating garbage unnecessarily.

questions.question: What is a good question to ask when designing a payment API or another important side effect?
answer: If the client sends the exact same request two or three more times, will the system repeat the side effect?
